title: Recall vector spaces, column space and nullspace

cards.front: Which two requirements make a set of vectors a vector space?
cards.back: Every sum $\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}$ and every multiple $c\mathbf{v}$ of its vectors stay in the set. So every linear combination stays in it, and $\mathbf{0}$ belongs to it.
$\mathbf{R}^3$ itself, every plane through $\mathbf{0}$, every line through $\mathbf{0}$, and $\mathbf{Z}$, the zero vector alone.

cards.front: Is the intersection of two subspaces a subspace? Is their union?
cards.back: The intersection always is. The union usually is not, because a vector of one plus a vector of the other can lie in neither.

cards.front: What is the column space $C(A)$ of an $m \times n$ matrix $A$?
cards.back: Every combination of the columns of $A$; these are exactly the vectors $A\mathbf{x}$. It is a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^m$.

cards.front: For which $\mathbf{b}$ does $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ have a solution?
cards.back: Exactly for $\mathbf{b}$ in $C(A)$. The weights of a combination of the columns that gives $\mathbf{b}$ form $\mathbf{x}$.

cards.front: What is the nullspace $N(A)$ of an $m \times n$ matrix $A$, and where does it lie?
cards.back: All solutions $\mathbf{x}$ of $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{0}$. It is a subspace of $\mathbf{R}^n$.
